question: scheduling assumptions audit — descriptive, not a production model change

window.removal_inference: no_longer_observed is inferred only on complete snapshots. Earlier unknown snapshots still record showtimes that were present.

end_weekday.population: Confirmed ends only: last occurred show is strictly before the theater dense horizon, and no later showtime remains on the schedule. Ordinary primary population also requires catalog segment=ordinary and span>=7 days. Rereleases and specials use catalog categories only; title disagreements are separate.

predetermined_engagements.population: Film×theater engagements whose first snapshot is after collection started, whose first showtime is after that snapshot, and whose end is confirmed. Share visible uses scheduled screenings that were already present on the first snapshot divided by scheduled screenings that remained (removals excluded from the denominator). Removal counts are a lower bound: the ledger only infers absence from complete snapshots.

capacity.population: Daily scheduled screenings that were not canceled and not removed before the show. Distribution stats use the continuous dense horizon only, so the unpublished tail does not look like a collapse in programming. Auditorium counts are parsed from the theater id.

displacement.population: Occurred Thursday→Friday pairs inside each theater's dense horizon. Incoming screenings are Friday screenings of films absent on Thursday. Incumbent screenings lost are Thursday screenings of films absent on Friday plus Thursday screenings dropped by films that continued with fewer shows.

contraction.population: Retrospective. Confirmed film×theater exits aligned on the last occurred show date. Days before the engagement started are omitted rather than treated as zero. Theater-count path is market-level ordinary week-plus exits.

completeness.population: For each observation date, upcoming Friday is the Friday on or after that date. The denominator is screenings on that Friday that were not removed before showtime and whose Friday is already in the past (as-of), so the set is closed. New vs continuing uses the market engagement's first Fri–Thu week. Retrospective.

candidate_implications.pattern: Ordinary film×theater runs end on Thursday
candidate_implications.evidence: Confirmed Thursday share=44.0% (n=336, Wilson low=38.8%). Wednesday share=53.6% (n=180). Publication-frontier n=0. Among theaters with n≥20, Thursday share ranges from 16.7% at AMC Oak Tree 6 (n=24) to 84.6% at AMC Factoria 8 (n=26).

candidate_implications.pattern: Ordinary week-plus film×theater runs end on Wednesday or Thursday
candidate_implications.evidence: Wednesday 53.6% (180) plus Thursday 44.0% (148) = 97.6% of n=336. Friday share=0.0%, Saturday=0.0%, Sunday=0.0%, Tuesday count=8.

candidate_implications.pattern: Rerelease schedules are fixed at announcement, unlike ordinary releases
candidate_implications.evidence: Catalog rereleases: median share visible at first observation=34.2%, extension rate=81.0%, n=63. Ordinary comparison median share=25.0%, n=315. Catalog specials, separately: median share visible=100.0%, extension rate=20.2%, n=282.

candidate_implications.pattern: Catalog special events are published in full when first observed
candidate_implications.evidence: Median share of eventual screenings visible at first observation=100.0%, extension rate=20.2%, n=282. Ordinary releases in the same filter: median share=25.0%, extension rate=74.6%, n=315.

candidate_implications.pattern: Within a weekday, theater screening volume is tight
candidate_implications.evidence: Median within-weekday coefficient of variation across theater×weekday cells=0.14 (cells=49).

candidate_implications.pattern: Incoming Friday screenings move with incumbent screenings lost
candidate_implications.evidence: Spearman r=0.47 across 91 theater-weeks. Association only.

candidate_implications.pattern: Screenings decline over the final week before a confirmed exit
candidate_implications.evidence: Median screenings D-7=3.0, D0=1.0, n=336. Retrospective alignment on the eventual end date.

candidate_implications.pattern: Missing next-week showtimes before Thursday can be unpublished schedule rather than an exit
candidate_implications.evidence: Pooled share of eventual upcoming-Friday screenings already known: Monday=37.7% (n=5157), Thursday=98.9% (n=5157). This describes publication cadence, not a film's remaining run.
